[F001] All work is complete and verified. Summary of how I addressed the audit finding:

**Finding [high, correctness] — D045 not satisfied for an installed/off-git package.** The auditor was correct: `release_manifest.py` resolved both the validation model and `docs/upgrade/releases.json` by walking `__file__` up to repo-root layouts (`claude/shared/...`, `docs/upgrade/...`), neither of which `pyproject.toml` packages — so a pip-installed wheel could not find them, and the only existing test merely changed cwd. I fixed this by genuinely making both resources package-relative and shipping them in the distribution:

- **Packaged the manifest as package data.** Added `scripts/dontpanic_orchestrate/data/releases.json` and declared `[tool.setuptools.package-data] dontpanic_orchestrate = ["data/*.json"]`. `load_release_manifest`/`default_manifest_path` now resolve it via `importlib.resources.files("dontpanic_orchestrate")` — no `__file__` walk, no cwd/git dependence. All the old `sys.path` schema-discovery hackery is gone.
- **Vendored the validation model into the package.** Added `scripts/dontpanic_orchestrate/upgrade_releases_model.py` and changed the loader (and tests) to import `from dontpanic_orchestrate.upgrade_releases_model`, so validation needs no repo-relative path injection. The agent-conventions mirror under `claude/shared/...` is kept (per plan + VERSION bump), guarded against drift by a byte-equality test.
- **Added the test the auditor asked for.** `test_loads_from_isolat
